relationships.explanation: The ratio between inner canthal distance and alar base width ideally approaches 1:1. A ratio of 1.38 indicates the nasal base extends beyond the medial canthi, creating visual width in the midface.
levers: Brow grooming to widen perceived eye spacing

relationships.impact: Slight vertical compression between nose base and lip creates a subtly shortened philtral impression.
relationships.explanation: The vermilion height to nasal length ratio indicates whether the lower midface reads proportional. At 0.48, the lips read slightly thin relative to nasal projection.
levers: Lip care routine to enhance definition

relationships.explanation: The bigonial to bizygomatic width ratio determines facial taper. At 0.82, the lower face reads marginally wider than optimal for a tapered silhouette.

relationships.impact: Upper third reads marginally short, shifting visual centre of gravity downward.
relationships.explanation: The trichion-to-glabella height as a proportion of total facial length. At 0.31, the upper third is slightly compressed compared to the classical ideal.

relationships.pair: Brow to Eye Distance : Eye Height
relationships.impact: Within tolerance band. Brow-to-lid proportion reads balanced.
relationships.explanation: The supraorbital-to-palpebral ratio measures the vertical space between brow ridge and upper eyelid relative to the palpebral fissure height. At 1.62, this falls squarely within the ideal band.

relationships.impact: Chin reads slightly recessed relative to lip projection, affecting lower profile balance.
relationships.explanation: Measured from the Ricketts E-line perspective, the chin-to-lip projection ratio indicates lower facial profile harmony. At 0.91, the chin sits marginally behind the ideal plane.
levers: Facial hair to adjust visual projection

expressionIndices.name: Softness vs Definition
expressionIndices.explanation: Structural configuration leans toward moderate softness in contour lines, driven by rounded mandibular angle and moderate buccal fullness. Definition reads most clearly at the brow ridge and nasal bridge.

expressionIndices.name: Warmth vs Intensity
expressionIndices.explanation: Features read as moderately warm. Larger palpebral fissure height and gentle canthal tilt contribute to an approachable structural read. Intensity is moderated by soft orbital framing.

expressionIndices.name: Masculine vs Feminine Spectrum
expressionIndices.explanation: Structural markers distribute near the androgynous midpoint. Brow ridge prominence and jaw width lean slightly masculine; lip fullness and eye shape provide balancing feminine structural cues.

metrics.name: Canthal Tilt
metrics.explanation: The angle from medial to lateral canthus. Within tolerance band at 4.2 degrees. Positive canthal tilt contributes to perceived alertness and youthful structure.

metrics.name: Palpebral Fissure Width
metrics.explanation: Horizontal eye opening width. At 28.1mm, falls within the normal range. Width interacts with interocular distance to determine midface proportional reading.

metrics.name: Upper Eyelid Exposure
metrics.explanation: Visible skin between brow and upper lid crease. At 2.8mm, proportional and indicating no significant ptosis or excess exposure.

metrics.name: Eye Spacing Ratio
metrics.explanation: Interocular distance as ratio of eye width. At 1.04, the spacing is within the golden proportion band.

metrics.name: Nasofrontal Angle
metrics.explanation: The angle at the junction of forehead and nasal dorsum. At 138 degrees, sits within the ideal range indicating smooth forehead-to-nose transition.

metrics.name: Nasal Bridge Width
metrics.explanation: Width at the narrowest point of the nasal dorsum. At 16.8mm, reads 6.1% wider than the upper tolerance band, contributing to visual width in the midface.

metrics.name: Nasal Tip Projection
metrics.explanation: Anterior projection of nasal tip from alar base plane. Within ideal band, contributing to balanced midface profile.

metrics.name: Alar Base Width
metrics.explanation: Width across nostril base. At 37.2mm, slightly exceeds the upper band. Interacts with interocular distance ratio.
levers: No structural change possible without intervention

metrics.name: Upper Lip Volume
metrics.explanation: Vertical height of upper vermilion. At 6.2mm, reads below ideal band. The upper-to-lower lip ratio is consequently shifted, affecting labial balance.

metrics.name: Vermilion Ratio
metrics.explanation: Upper to lower lip height ratio. At 0.58, indicates relative upper lip thinness. Ideally the upper lip is 65-75% of lower lip height.

metrics.name: Philtrum Length
metrics.explanation: Distance from nasal base to upper lip border. At 14.8mm, within tolerance but at the upper end, which can reduce perceived lip prominence.

metrics.name: Facial Width-Height Ratio
metrics.explanation: Bizygomatic width to nasion-gnathion height. At 1.88, squarely within the golden proportion band for facial rectangularity.

metrics.name: Cheekbone Prominence
metrics.explanation: Relative zygomatic projection. At 71, reads at the lower end of ideal. Adequate but not prominent, creating a subtler midface contour.

metrics.name: Mandibular Angle
metrics.explanation: Angle at the mandibular gonion. At 122 degrees, within range. Contributes to the moderate softness in jawline definition.

metrics.name: Jawline Definition
metrics.explanation: Overall jawline sharpness and cervical definition. At 64, reads below ideal, likely due to submental fullness or soft tissue laxity obscuring the mandibular border.

metrics.name: Chin Projection
metrics.explanation: Anterior chin projection relative to the Ricketts E-line. At 88%, the chin reads as mildly recessed, affecting lower facial profile balance.

metrics.name: Facial Thirds - Upper
metrics.explanation: Upper third (trichion to glabella) proportion. At 31.2%, slightly compressed. This shifts the visual centre of gravity downward.

metrics.name: Facial Thirds - Middle
metrics.explanation: Middle third (glabella to subnasale) reads slightly elongated at 35.6%. This is the most common deviation pattern and affects midface proportion.

metrics.name: Facial Thirds - Lower
metrics.explanation: Lower third (subnasale to menton) at 33.2% falls within the ideal band. Good vertical proportion in the lower face.

metrics.name: Golden Ratio Adherence
metrics.explanation: Composite score measuring adherence to phi (1.618) across multiple facial proportion pairs. At 78, indicates moderate alignment with classical proportional ideals.

metrics.name: Vertical Symmetry
metrics.explanation: Bilateral vertical alignment of paired features. At 93.2%, a slight but normal asymmetry exists, most visible in the orbital region.

metrics.name: Horizontal Symmetry
metrics.explanation: Bilateral horizontal alignment. At 94.8%, essentially within tolerance. Minor asymmetry is biologically expected and often imperceptible.

metrics.name: Texture Uniformity
metrics.explanation: Surface texture evenness across facial zones. At 76, mild textural inconsistency in the T-zone. This is the most changeable skin metric.

metrics.name: Tone Evenness
metrics.explanation: Chromatic consistency across facial surface. At 80, sits at the lower edge of ideal with mild perioral variation noted.

metrics.name: Overall Radiance
metrics.explanation: Surface luminosity and light reflection quality. At 72, suggests mild barrier compromise or dehydration affecting skin's optical properties.

metrics.name: Under-Eye Area
metrics.explanation: Periorbital skin quality including hollowing, pigmentation, and puffiness assessment. At 68, mild infraorbital shadowing present, likely circulatory or genetic in origin.

metrics.name: Lip Symmetry
metrics.explanation: Bilateral labial symmetry. At 91%, a slight asymmetry in commissure height. Common and rarely perceptible in motion.

metrics.name: Brow Symmetry
metrics.explanation: Bilateral eyebrow position and shape symmetry. At 89%, slight height difference between left and right brow. Highly correctable through grooming.

recommendations.title: Skincare foundation protocol
steps: Introduce gentle cleanser (pH 5.5)
Layer hyaluronic acid on damp skin
Apply niacinamide 10% serum
Seal with ceramide moisturiser
SPF 50 every morning without exception

recommendations.title: Brow architecture optimisation
steps: Map brows using nose-bridge alignment method
Address height asymmetry by removing 1-2mm from higher brow
Clean below arch line only
Maintain natural thickness — avoid over-plucking
Brush upward daily with clear gel

recommendations.title: Jawline definition programme
steps: Reduce overall body fat percentage by 3-5%
Mewing technique: tongue posture against palate
Jaw resistance exercises 3x weekly
Gua sha along mandibular border daily
Improve posture — forward head posture worsens cervical definition

recommendations.title: Lip care and definition routine
steps: Exfoliate lips weekly with sugar scrub
Apply peptide lip treatment nightly
Hydrate with hyaluronic acid lip product
SPF lip balm during day
Avoid licking — compromises barrier

recommendations.title: Hairstyle optimisation for facial framing
steps: Add volume at crown to compensate upper third compression
Avoid flat styles that emphasise forehead proportion
Side-part to create asymmetric visual interest
Texture at temples to soften jaw-width perception
Consult stylist with reference to face-shape framing

recommendations.title: Sleep and recovery optimisation
steps: Target 7-9 hours consistently
Sleep on back to prevent facial compression asymmetry
Elevate head slightly to reduce periorbital puffiness
No screens 1 hour before bed
Cool, dark room — melatonin optimisation

recommendations.title: Advanced retinoid introduction
steps: Start with 0.025% tretinoin or adapalene
Apply pea-sized amount every 3rd night initially
Buffer with moisturiser first for 4 weeks
Increase to alternate nights after 6 weeks
Mandatory SPF — photosensitivity is real

recommendations.title: Hydration and nutrition protocol
steps: Minimum 2.5L water daily
Omega-3 supplementation (fish oil or algae)
Reduce refined sugar — glycation ages skin
Collagen peptide supplementation (5-10g daily)
Antioxidant-rich diet — berries, green tea, dark vegetables
